battle.name: 范延堡之戰
battle.brief: 一二二一年七月二十七日，法王腓力二世在佛蘭德斯范延堡迎擊神聖羅馬皇帝奧托四世與英格蘭王約翰的北方聯軍。聯軍右翼陷於濕地泥濘，中央被法軍重騎反衝崩潰，奧托與布洛涅伯爵威廉重傷被俘，朗斯佩伯爵率英軍突圍而走，聯盟就此瓦解。卡面的十字弩是聯軍前鋒的射擊主力，中央一崩潰便無從退走。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 范延堡之戰的交戰雙方，是法蘭西王國的國王軍與北方反法聯軍。聯軍以神聖羅馬帝國皇帝奧托四世為核心，聯合英格蘭王國、佛蘭德斯伯爵領的諸侯、荷蘭伯爵威廉二世、據說還有丹麥王瓦爾德馬二世所遣的援軍，以及普瓦捷的呂西尼家族。英格蘭的野戰指揮權交在薩利伯蘭伯爵威廉·朗斯佩手裡，他帶來三百至四百名騎士與上千名步兵弓箭手、弩手；佛蘭德斯與不列顛各城的民兵由布洛涅伯爵威廉率領；德意志與薩克森的騎士在皇帝本人旗幟下集結；呂西尼伯爵休十世把普瓦捷的貴族與生力軍拉上來，荷蘭伯爵威廉二世與呂西尼家族都站在法國王室的對面。法軍由法王腓力二世親自統率，骨幹是王家騎士團與兩支王家大公司，其中一支部由紀堯姆·德普萊率領，步兵以巴黎與各地城鎮民兵充之，王旗奧里弗拉姆由國王近衛高擎，作為全軍效忠的目標。戰場在佛蘭德斯伯國范延堡村北，夾在土爾內與里爾之間的濕地與農地，控住土爾內通往康布雷的通道；聯軍若勝，等於把英格蘭在普瓦捷的戰線與北方反叛諸侯接成一氣，所以雙方都把此役當成整個西歐格局的一次攤牌。
countriesEn: The two sides in the battle of Bouvines were the royal army of the kingdom of France and an anti-French coalition from the north. At the heart of the coalition stood the Holy Roman Emperor Otto IV, joined by the kingdom of England, the barons of the county of Flanders, William II count of Holland, a contingent said to have been sent by the Danish king Valdemar II, and the Lusignan family of Poitou. The field command on the English side lay with William Longespée, earl of Salisbury, who brought three to four hundred knights together with more than a thousand foot archers and crossbowmen; the levies of the Flemish and other British towns were led by William count of Boulogne; the knights of Germany and Saxony were assembled under the emperor's own banner; and Hugh X count of Lusignan brought the nobles and the fighting men of Poitou, with William II of Holland and the Lusignans standing on the side opposed to the French king. The French army was commanded by King Philip II in person. Its backbone was the royal household knights and the two great companies of arms, one of which was led by Guillaume des Prés; its foot was made up of the militia of Paris and of the other towns; and the Oriflamme was raised on a high pole by the king's close guard as the point toward which the whole army was to look. The field lay north of the village of Bouvines in the county of Flanders, among the marshes and farmland between Tournai and Lille, commanding the road from Tournai toward Cambrai. Had the coalition won, the northern rebels and the English front in Poitou would have been joined into one, and so both sides treated this battle as the settling of the whole order of western Europe.
people: 法方是法王腓力二世本人。他一一八〇年以十四歲之齡即位，到一二二一年已統王四十一年，把王室直屬地從小科爾貝擴張到諾曼第、奧爾良與香檹，凡爾賽成為固定的御前駐地；此役是他第一次把王軍、外州貴族與北方盟主的軍隊在同一戰場上混編使用，也是他一生中少數親自站在最前線的野戰。英格蘭方面的關鍵人物是薩利伯蘭伯爵威廉·朗斯佩——約翰王的庶子，綽號「長劍」；他以父親使者的身分遊說北方諸侯，替英格蘭拉來德意志與佛蘭德斯的援兵，並在聯軍中握有實際的戰術指揮權。他在范延堡的右翼崩潰後，靠英格蘭弩手與佛蘭德斯輕騎遮斷才殺出重圍，隨後退回普瓦捷，最終死於一二二六年拉羅什莫因的圍城之中。聯軍名義上的統帥是神聖羅馬皇帝奧托四世，他本人在混戰中被法軍騎士砍傷並被俘，直到一二二二年才以放棄洛林公國予其弟腓特烈為條件獲釋。布洛涅伯爵威廉是法國貴族出身卻站在聯軍一邊的人物，任聯軍右翼主將，與奧托同樣負傷被俘。另有史料記載薩克森公爵「獅子亨利」參戰並於戰後被俘、其後獲釋；荷蘭伯爵威廉二世與呂西尼伯爵休十世同樣淪為俘虜。留下最完整戰場記錄的是英格蘭修士羅傑·溫多佛，法方則有威廉·布列塔尼以拉丁長詩《菲利普斯》歌詠此役。
peopleEn: On the French side was King Philip II himself. He had taken the throne in 1180 at the age of fourteen, and by 1221 he had ruled for forty-one years, enlarging the royal domain from the small Capetian core through Normandy, Orléans and Champagne and fixing his court at Versailles; this was the first time he put the royal army, the nobles of the outer provinces and the contingents of his northern allies into the same battle, and it was one of the few occasions in his life when he stood in the front of a pitched battle himself. The key figure on the English side was William Longespée, earl of Salisbury, the natural son of King John, nicknamed Longsword; he acted as his father's envoy to the princes of the north, drew German and Flemish succour to England, and held the real tactical command in the coalition. When his flank gave way at Bouvines he cut his way out with the English crossbowmen and light Flemish horse and withdrew into Poitou, where he finally died in the siege of La Roche-au-Moine in 1226. The nominal commander of the coalition was the Holy Roman Emperor Otto IV, who was cut down by French knights in the mêlée and taken prisoner, and who was not released until 1222, when he renounced the duchy of Lorraine to his brother Frederick. William of Boulogne, a man of French birth who had thrown in his lot with the coalition, commanded the right wing and was wounded and captured like the emperor. The records also carry a story that Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony, took part and was captured afterwards and later set free; William II of Holland and Hugh X of Lusignan likewise ended up in captivity. The fullest account of the field is that of the English friar Roger of Wendover, and on the French side William of Brittany sang the campaign in the Latin poem of the Philippide.
kits: 本卡的兵器是十字弩，一二二一年在聯軍裡主要由英格蘭與佛蘭德斯的步兵弩手使用，當時它仍是野戰中最不像主流的冷兵器：英格蘭與威爾斯長弓手名聲在外，弩在英格蘭軍隊中則是編制較小、射速較慢，但穿透力與精度更穩的一支。十字弩的結構在十二世紀末已大致定型：木製弩身、弩臂、弦、扳機與弦鉤，弩手以蹺板、絞盤或起重式的「克蘭克」張弦，一般的「克雷內爾」型弩臂用木與角製作，弦鉤則要在放矢後重新咬合。獅子心形的拉弦器要到十三世紀末至十四世紀才逐漸普及，一二二一年的弩仍多靠手與蹺板完成張弦，一個熟手弩手每分鐘只能放數箭，這就是本卡那句「裝填慢」的實情。放矢之後弩手便無從自衛，所以弩手必須排成密集方陣，置於騎兵之前，用以在敵騎衝鋒之前射開對方的正面，或在敵軍逼近時轉成掩體。范延堡的地面對弩手有利也對弩手不利：濕地與壕溝擋住騎兵的衝鋒，給了弩手更多射擊時間；但一旦聯軍中央被突破，弩陣失去騎兵遮蔽，弩手與馬匹混在一起奔逃，成了最容易被追殺的一群。兩軍的其他裝備包括長劍、騎槍、鎖子甲、盾牌與戰旗，奧里弗拉姆作為王旗被視為國王本人在場的憑證；英格蘭與佛蘭德斯的聯軍還備有車列與隨軍輜重車，用以攔截法軍側翼的穿插。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the crossbow, and in 1221 it was used in the coalition chiefly by the foot crossbowmen of the English and the Flemings. Even then it was the least usual of the missile weapons in the field: the longbowmen of England and Wales were famous, while the crossbow in the English army formed a smaller body, slower in rate of fire but steadier in accuracy and penetration. By the end of the twelfth century the form of the crossbow had settled: a wooden stock, the bow, the string, the trigger and the nut, with the string drawn by a treadle, a windlass or, for the heavier pieces, a rack-and-pinion crane; the ordinary crenell type used a bow of wood and horn, and the nut had to be re-engaged after every shot. The goat's-foot lever that made the weapon quick to reload did not become common until the late thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, so the crossbow of 1221 was still cocked by hand and treadle, and a practised crossbowman could loose only a few bolts a minute; that is the truth of the card's line that the rate of fire was given over to a machine at the price of slow loading. Once the bolt was away the crossbowman could not defend himself, so the crossbowmen had to stand in close order in front of the horse, to open up the face of the enemy before his charge came, or to form a shelter when the enemy closed. The ground at Bouvines was favourable to the crossbowmen and unfavourable to them at once: the wet ground and the ditches slowed the charges of the cavalry and gave the crossbowmen more time to shoot, but once the centre of the coalition had broken and the crossbow ranks had lost the cover of the horse, the loose bolts had no way back and the men and horses ran mingled, the easiest of all to run down. The rest of the equipment on both sides was the sword, the lance, the mail hauberk, the shield and the banner, with the Oriflamme carried as the visible sign of the king in person; the English and Flemish coalition also had waggons and baggage train with it, to close the flank against French turns.
tactics: 這一役的戰術，兩邊都犯了同一種毛病，只是方向相反。聯軍在范延堡村北選了靠土爾內的一側宿營，前夜在通往土爾內的大路旁掘了一道壕溝（法蘭西北方傳說稱「王的壕溝」，兩役的壕線是否同一條，史料說法不一），以木板小橋跨越，企圖用濕地與泥濘擋住法軍的騎兵衝鋒，再在平地上以密集的德意志與佛蘭德斯重騎迎擊。問題出在聯軍自己的指揮上：英格蘭修士羅傑·溫多佛記錄，聯軍內部在出戰前為統率權爭執不下，英格蘭人自恃帶來人數最多、要求由英格蘭方面執旗，荷蘭與佛蘭德斯的諸侯不服，陣形因此拖到法軍逼近才完成部署，騎兵有相當一段時間沒有列成線，壕溝兩側的步兵也沒有同時接敵。英格蘭與佛蘭德斯的弩手，以及一部分長弓手，依例排在聯軍兩翼與前鋒之前，計畫以射擊削弱法軍前鋒的密集步兵，再讓己方重騎趁隙反衝；然而左翼與中央一旦被突破，弩陣既無馬可乘、又無盾可結，隨即被法軍騎兵衝散，弩手的潰逃成了聯軍崩潰的引線。法軍這邊，腓力二世把王旗奧里弗拉姆置於中軍，率王家騎士團與大公司正面推向壕溝，先以步兵與少量弩手在泥濘裡消耗聯軍前鋒，待聯軍重騎自側翼包抄而露出缺口，王家重騎才在狹窄地段一齊發力；側翼的迂迴兵力（來自皮卡第與佛蘭德斯的城鎮民兵）繞過壕溝端頭，從側後包抄，把潰退中的聯軍堵在濕地裡。兩軍自清晨打到午後，戰場喊聲是法軍的「蒙若耶與聖但尼」與聯軍的「聖喬治」，旗幟與旗幟之間的接觸幾次中斷又接上。最後以法軍的全面反衝收場，聯軍中央先崩，兩翼隨之瓦解，奧托與威廉被圍在中軍，才被生擒。
tacticsEn: The two sides made the same sort of mistake on this field, only in opposite directions. The coalition camped on the Tournai side north of the village of Bouvines and in the night before the battle dug a ditch along the road to Tournai, known in the country of the north of France as the fossé du roi, with a plank bridge over it, meaning to use the wet ground and the mud to hold off the French cavalry and then meet them on the open with a solid mass of German and Flemish heavy horse. What went wrong was the command of the coalition itself. Roger of Wendover records that the English, who brought the largest contingent, claimed the banner and the command of the whole army, while the princes of Holland and Flanders would not accept it, and the argument held up the deployment until the French were close at hand; for a good part of the time the heavy horse was not drawn up in line, and the foot on the two sides of the ditch did not engage all at once. Following the custom of the age, the English and Flemish crossbowmen, with a part of the longbowmen, were posted at the front and on the wings of the coalition, to wear down the dense French vanguard with their shooting and then let the heavy horse charge into the gap; but when the left wing and the centre were broken, the crossbow ranks had neither horse to ride nor shield to lock, and they scattered as the French horse came through them, and the flight of the crossbowmen was the fuse of the collapse of the coalition. On the French side Philip II put the Oriflamme in the centre and led the household knights and the great companies straight at the ditch, first spending the French foot and a few crossbowmen in the mud against the front of the coalition, and then, when the coalition heavy horse came round the flank and left a gap, committing the royal heavy horse in one push on the narrow ground; the columns that turned the position, drawn from the towns of Picardy and Flanders, went round the end of the ditch and came at the flank and the rear, and shut the retreating coalition up in the wet ground. The two sides fought from early morning into the afternoon, the cries were Montjoie and Saint Denis on the French side and Saint George on the other, and the contact between the banners was broken and made again several times. It ended with the general French counter-charge: the centre of the coalition gave way first, the wings followed, and Otto and William were taken in the midst of their own host.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間：一二二一年七月二十七日交戰，據編年史記述，戰鬥自清晨打到午後，歷時數小時。地名：戰場在今法國北部諾爾省范延堡村一帶，位於土爾內東南約十公里、里爾以北約二十公里，村北的沼澤地與農地之間有一條自東南流向西北的水溝。兵力：法軍出動的總數沒有可靠記載，後世史家一般估計在六千至八千人之間，其中騎兵約二千至三千；聯軍總數通常被認為在萬人至一萬四千人上下，明確可考的只有英格蘭一支——英格蘭編年史的說法是三百至四百名騎士，外加一千至一千二百名步兵弓箭手與弩手。羅傑·溫多佛與其他中世紀編年史的數字普遍被後世認定為夸大，不宜照引。損耗：聯軍中央與左翼被法軍重騎反覆衝擊，英格蘭與佛蘭德斯的旗手與貴族大量淪為俘虜，僅少數得以脫身，騎士俘虜達數百人，多數以贖金或交還土地換回自由。俘虜名單中有神聖羅馬皇帝奧托四世、布洛涅伯爵威廉、荷蘭伯爵威廉二世、呂西尼伯爵休十世，另有薩克森公爵「獅子亨利」被俘的記載。戰後安排：奧托四世被囚約一年，至一二二二年以放棄洛林公國予其弟腓特烈為條件獲釋。相關事件：法軍另一支由王弟路易八世率領的部隊在同一個七月拿下了英格蘭在普瓦捷的拉羅什莫因城堡，時間是七月二日，早於此戰三週；同年英格蘭王約翰的普瓦捷遠征失敗。最後，戰場上兩軍實際接觸的正面不過一公里多的寬度，聯軍雖排得寬，中央與左翼同時崩潰，整條戰線便作廢。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. In time: the battle was fought on the twenty-seventh day of July 1221, and the chroniclers describe the fighting as running from early morning into the afternoon over a matter of hours. In place: the field lies around the village of Bouvines in the département of Nord in the north of modern France, some ten kilometres south-east of Tournai and about twenty kilometres north of Lille, with a watercourse running from south-east to north-west through the marshes and fields north of the village. In strength: there is no reliable figure for the French army, and modern historians generally put it at between six and eight thousand men, of whom two to three thousand were mounted; the coalition is usually put at ten to fourteen thousand, and the only contingent that can be given with any clarity is the English, which the English chronicles describe as three to four hundred knights with a thousand to twelve hundred foot archers and crossbowmen. The figures of Roger of Wendover and the other medieval chroniclers are generally held by later scholarship to be inflated and are not to be quoted as they stand. In losses: the centre and the left wing of the coalition were struck again and again by the French heavy horse, and the gonfaloners and nobles of England and Flanders were taken in great numbers, only a few escaping; several hundred knights were captured, and most of them bought their freedom by ransom or by the surrender of land. Among the prisoners were the Holy Roman Emperor Otto IV, William of Boulogne, William II of Holland and Hugh X of Lusignan, and there is a record of Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony, being captured as well. In the settlement after the battle: Otto IV was held about a year and was released in 1222 on condition of renouncing the duchy of Lorraine to his brother Frederick. In related events: another French force under the king's brother Louis VIII took the English castle of La Roche-au-Moine in Poitou in the same month of July, on the second of the month, three weeks before this battle, and John's own expedition into Poitou failed in the same year. Finally, the front on which the two armies actually touched was little more than a kilometre and a half wide; the coalition was drawn up much wider, but the centre and the left wing broke together, and the whole line was wasted.
cause: 打起嚟的緣由，是英格蘭王約翰在歐陸的處境與法國王室的擴張正面撞在一起。一二二○年前後，普瓦捷的呂西尼家族以休十世為首起兵反約翰，得到法國的暗中支持；約翰在一二二一年春親率大軍渡海登陸普瓦捷，企圖把這一區重新控制住，卻在布列塔尼與拉羅什莫因一線受挫，攻勢停在土爾內以北，於是把希望寄在北方盟友身上。北方自一二一四年范延堡的敗績之後，許多佛蘭德斯、荷蘭與德意志的諸侯一直想把那年輸掉的局面翻回去；約翰在北方也有自己的盤算——他需要一個足以威脅法王室的聯盟，來解普瓦捷之圍。英格蘭與北方諸侯在約翰的使節（包括他自己的庶子朗斯佩）穿梭之下組成聯軍，神聖羅馬皇帝奧托四世也在其中；聯軍的目標是打穿法王室的北方防線，讓佛蘭德斯的諸侯重新回到各自領主的旗下，並使英格蘭在普瓦捷的戰線得到喘息。問題在於聯軍本身不具備協同作戰的條件：皇帝財政吃緊，欠餉與缺糧的傳聞在出戰前就已傳遍營地，荷蘭、佛蘭德斯與英格蘭各有各的算盤，所謂共同戰線其實只是各懷目的的臨時拼湊。腓力二世把握了這一點：他沒有坐等聯軍合圍，而是把主力西進、留北方少量兵力周旋，同時讓路易八世在普瓦捷方向施加壓力，逼聯軍必須速戰速決。
causeEn: The war came out of the fact that the position of King John in continental Europe and the expansion of the French royal house had come into direct collision. Around 1220 the Lusignans of Poitou, headed by Hugh X, rose against John with the quiet support of France; John crossed the sea in person in the spring of 1221 with a great army to try to win that province back, was checked on the line of Brittany and La Roche-au-Moine, and his advance stalled north of Tours, so he set his hopes on his allies in the north. Since the defeat at Bouvines in 1214 the princes of Flanders, Holland and Germany had been trying to undo the result of that year, and John had his own calculation in the north as well: he needed a coalition strong enough to threaten the royal house of France and to relieve his position in Poitou. With John's envoys, his natural son Longespée among them, moving between the courts, the league of England and the northern princes was formed, and the Holy Roman Emperor Otto IV was in it. The aim of the coalition was to break the northern defences of the French king, to bring the Flemish barons back under their own lords, and to give the English front in Poitou a chance to breathe. The trouble was that the coalition had no capacity for joint action: the emperor was in financial distress, and talk of unpaid wages and short rations was already going round the camp before the army moved, while Holland, Flanders and England each had their own arithmetic, and the common front was in truth a temporary patchwork of men with separate purposes. Philip II understood this. He did not wait for the coalition to close around him: he took the bulk of his force west against Poitou, left only a small force to contain the north, and used the pressure of Louis VIII in Poitou to force the coalition to fight before it was ready.
impact: 范延堡之戰的影響，落在三個層面。第一層是英格蘭與北方聯盟：聯盟被打散，佛蘭德斯的諸侯陸續回到女伯爵胡安娜的權威之下，荷蘭與薩克森的諸侯各自求和，約翰在歐陸的外交從此只剩一條路——向法王俯首；他在法國的殘餘領地退到吉倫特與波爾多一線，這條線一直維持到一二五九年《巴黎條約》才被正式放棄。聯軍在北方的軍事意義此後數十年內消失，直到一二九七年英格蘭的愛德華一世再糾集佛蘭德斯諸侯南下，才重演類似局面，並在一三○二年金馬刺之役中敗得更慘。第二層是法蘭西王室的國家化：腓力二世把北法蘭西的實際控制與海上的補給通道同時鞏固，諾曼第、貝里、奧爾良與香檹的貴族以各種名義陸續歸附王室直屬地，凡爾賽成為常設的御前駐地；他在范延堡的勝利與一二二六年路易八世戰死於曼西十字軍之後的權力集中相接起來，法國的君主制在這十年間完成了一次質的變化。第三層是帝國的走向：奧托四世被囚近一年，選帝問題與洛林公國的歸屬同時被推遲，他弟弟腓特烈藉機接下洛林，把南義大利與德意志的聯姻線握在手中，數年後成為教皇與皇帝鬥爭裡的另一方。對兵器史而言，此役是弩手在野戰中的一次示範：濕地與壕溝把騎兵衝鋒壓慢，弩手因此得到寶貴的射擊時間；但同樣是濕地，一旦聯軍的中央被突破、弩陣失去騎兵遮護，弩手便無從自保——弩在野戰中的位置，本質上仍然被裝填速度綁在別人的馬上。戰場舊址在十九世紀中葉立了石碑，這場規模不算最大的戰役因此留在法國北部的鄉土記憶裡。
impactEn: The effect of the battle of Bouvines worked on three levels. The first was England and the northern coalition: the league was broken up, the Flemish barons returned one by one to the authority of the countess Joan of Flanders, the princes of Holland and Saxony made their peace each in his own way, and John's diplomacy in the continent was left with a single road, which was to bow to the king of France. His remaining French lands shrank to the strip of Garonne and Bordeaux, and that line was not given up formally until the Treaty of Paris in 1259. The military meaning of the northern coalition was not to return for several decades; it was not until 1297, when Edward I of England gathered the Flemish barons south again, that a similar situation was recreated, and it ended far worse at the Battle of the Golden Spurs in 1302. The second level was the state-making of the French monarchy: Philip II secured at once the practical control of northern France and the supply route by sea; the nobles of Normandy, Berry, Orléans and Champagne came over to the royal domain one after another under one name or another, and Versailles became the fixed seat of the court; the victory at Bouvines joined on to the concentration of power that followed the death of Louis VIII on crusade at Mansurah in 1226, and in those ten years the French monarchy changed its nature. The third level was the direction of the empire: Otto IV was held for nearly a year, the question of the election and the ownership of Lorraine were both deferred and rewritten, and his brother Frederick took Lorraine and so held the marriage lines of southern Italy and Germany in his own hands, a few years later becoming the other party in the quarrel between pope and emperor. For the history of weapons the battle is a demonstration of the crossbow in the open field: the wet ground and the ditches slow the charge and so give the crossbowman time to shoot, but the same wet ground, once the centre has broken and the crossbow ranks have lost the cover of the horse, leaves them without protection; the place of the crossbow in the field was bound in the end to someone else's horse by the speed of loading. A stone was set up on the old field in the middle of the nineteenth century, and this battle, not among the largest, has stayed in the local memory of the north of France.
result: 七月廿七日，聯軍尚未完成陣形便迎來法軍的正面推進。壕溝與濕地拖慢了法軍的騎兵，也把聯軍前鋒與弩手、步兵的距離拉長；法軍步兵與弩手先在泥濘裡與聯軍前鋒互相消耗，聯軍重騎自側翼繞出的時候，中央已失其銳。接著是法軍王旗奧里弗拉姆所指的全面反衝：王家騎士團與兩支大公司一齊壓上，聯軍中央的旗幟先倒，英格蘭與佛蘭德斯的方陣被切斷，包圍了聯軍的右翼。奧托四世在混戰中受傷倒地，與布洛涅伯爵威廉一同被法軍擄獲，並於同日被送往巴黎；荷蘭伯爵威廉二世、呂西尼伯爵休十世、薩克森公爵「獅子亨利」亦在俘獲名單之內。聯軍的左翼與大部分步兵被封在濕地與村莊之間，無路可退而被大量殺傷與俘虜，英格蘭與佛蘭德斯的旗手與貴族大量淪為俘虜。薩利伯蘭伯爵威廉·朗斯佩帶著英格蘭的核心人馬與一部分弩手殺出重圍，退回普瓦捷，之後投入對拉羅什莫因的戰事，最終死於那場圍城的攻城器械之下。戰果的政治意義大於戰術意義：北方聯盟此後再無力進攻法王室的北翼，英格蘭的普瓦捷反攻在同年秋被平定，呂西尼與其他普瓦捷貴族向路易八世歸順。此役同時也是弩手體系的一次失敗示範——聯軍把大量射擊兵擺在陣前，卻沒有留出退得回去的通道，裝填慢的弱點在中央崩潰時暴露無遺。
resultEn: On the twenty-seventh of July the coalition had not completed its formation before the French advance came on. The ditches and the wet ground slowed the French horse and stretched the distance between the front of the coalition and its crossbowmen and foot; the French foot and crossbowmen first wore each other out in the mud, and by the time the coalition heavy horse came round the flank the centre had already lost its edge. Then came the general French counter-charge under the Oriflamme: the royal household knights and the two great companies pressed home together, the banners of the centre of the coalition went down first, the English and Flemish squares were cut apart, and the right wing of the coalition was surrounded. Otto IV was struck down in the mêlée and taken with William of Boulogne, and they were carried off to Paris on the same day; William II of Holland, Hugh X of Lusignan and Henry the Lion were in the list of the captured as well. The left wing of the coalition and the greater part of its foot were shut up between the wet ground and the villages, and being without a way out they were killed and taken in great numbers, and the gonfaloners and nobles of England and Flanders were captured in heaps. William Longespée cut his way out with the core of the English and a part of the crossbowmen, withdrew into Poitou, and was drawn into the fighting over La Roche-au-Moine, where he finally died under the siege engines of that siege in 1226. The political meaning of the result was greater than its tactical meaning: the northern coalition was never again able to attack the northern flank of the French royal house, the English counter-offensive in Poitou was settled in the autumn of the same year, and the Lusignans and the other Poitevin nobles submitted to Louis VIII. The battle was at the same time a failure demonstrated in the system of the crossbowmen: the coalition put a mass of missile troops at the front of the line and left them no way back, and the weakness that comes from slow loading was laid bare when the centre broke.
